shlokas.sanskrit: ते प्रयाता महात्मानः पार्थिवास्ते प्रहृष्टवत् । गजवाजिसहस्रौघैः कम्पयन्तो वसुन्धराम् ।। 7.39.1 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: te prayātā mahātmānaḥ pārthivāste prahṛṣṭavat | gajavājisahasraughaiḥ kampayanto vasundharām || 7.39.1 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Those high-souled kings set forth in great joy, making the earth tremble beneath the floods of their thousands of elephants and horses.

shlokas.sanskrit: अक्षौहिण्यो हि तत्रासन्राघवार्थे समुद्यताः । भरतस्याज्ञया ऽनेकाः प्रहृष्टा बलवाहनाः ।। 7.39.2 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: akṣauhiṇyo hi tatrāsanrāghavārthe samudyatāḥ | bharatasyājñayā 'nekāḥ prahṛṣṭā balavāhanāḥ || 7.39.2 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: For many divisions of troops (akshauhinis), with their delighted forces and mounts, had been mustered there for Raghava's sake at Bharata's command.

shlokas.sanskrit: ऊचुस्ते च महीपाला बलदर्पसमन्विताः । न रामरावणं युद्धे पश्यामः पुरतः स्थितम् ।। 7.39.3 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: ūcuste ca mahīpālā baladarpasamanvitāḥ | na rāmarāvaṇaṃ yuddhe paśyāmaḥ purataḥ sthitam || 7.39.3 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: And those rulers of the earth, filled with pride in their strength, said: "We did not see the battle of Rama and Ravana take place before us."

shlokas.sanskrit: भरतेन वयं पश्चात्समानीता निरर्थकम् । हता हि राक्षसाः क्षिप्रं पार्थिवैः स्युर्न संशयः ।। 7.39.4 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: bharatena vayaṃ paścātsamānītā nirarthakam | hatā hi rākṣasāḥ kṣipraṃ pārthivaiḥ syurna saṃśayaḥ || 7.39.4 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: "To no purpose have we been brought along afterward by Bharata; for the Rakshasas would surely and swiftly have been slain by us kings, there is no doubt of it."

shlokas.sanskrit: रामस्य बाहुवीर्येण रक्षिता लक्ष्मणस्य च । सुखं पारेसमुद्रस्य युध्येम विगतज्वराः ।। 7.39.5 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: rāmasya bāhuvīryeṇa rakṣitā lakṣmaṇasya ca | sukhaṃ pāresamudrasya yudhyema vigatajvarāḥ || 7.39.5 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: "Guarded by the strength of Rama's arm and of Lakshmana's, we might easily and without distress have fought even beyond the ocean."

shlokas.sanskrit: एताश्चान्याश्च राजानः कथास्तत्र सहस्रशः । कथयन्तः स्वराज्यानि जग्मुर्हर्षसमन्विताः ।। 7.39.6 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: etāścānyāśca rājānaḥ kathāstatra sahasraśaḥ | kathayantaḥ svarājyāni jagmurharṣasamanvitāḥ || 7.39.6 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Telling these and other tales by the thousands there, the kings, filled with joy, departed to their own realms.

shlokas.sanskrit: स्वानि राज्यानि मुख्यानि ऋद्धानि मुदितानि च । समृद्धधनधान्यानि पूर्णानि वसुमन्ति च ।। 7.39.7 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: svāni rājyāni mukhyāni ṛddhāni muditāni ca | samṛddhadhanadhānyāni pūrṇāni vasumanti ca || 7.39.7 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Their own kingdoms were foremost, prosperous and joyful, abounding in wealth and grain, full and rich in treasure.

shlokas.sanskrit: यथापुराणि ते गत्वा रत्नानि विविधान्यथ । रामस्य प्रियकामार्थमुपहारान् नृपा ददुः ।। 7.39.8 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: yathāpurāṇi te gatvā ratnāni vividhānyatha | rāmasya priyakāmārthamupahārān nṛpā daduḥ || 7.39.8 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Then, having reached their own cities, those kings sent jewels of many kinds and gifts to please Rama and gratify his desire.

shlokas.sanskrit: अश्वान्यानानि रत्नानि हस्तिनश्च मदोत्कटान् । चन्दनानि च मुख्यानि दिव्यान्याभरणानि च ।। 7.39.9 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: aśvānyānāni ratnāni hastinaśca madotkaṭān | candanāni ca mukhyāni divyānyābharaṇāni ca || 7.39.9 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Horses, conveyances, jewels, elephants rutting with frenzy, the finest sandalwood, and divine ornaments,

shlokas.sanskrit: मणिमुक्ताप्रवालांस्तु दास्यो रूपसमन्विताः । अजाविकांश्च विविधान् रथांस्तु विविधान्ददुः ।। 7.39.10 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: maṇimuktāpravālāṃstu dāsyo rūpasamanvitāḥ | ajāvikāṃśca vividhān rathāṃstu vividhāndaduḥ || 7.39.10 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: gems, pearls, and corals, and handmaidens endowed with beauty, goats and sheep of many kinds, and chariots of various sorts they gave.

shlokas.sanskrit: भरतो लक्ष्मणश्चैव शत्रुघ्नश्च महाबलाः । आदाय तानि रत्नानि स्वां पुरीं पुनरागताः ।। 7.39.11 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: bharato lakṣmaṇaścaiva śatrughnaśca mahābalāḥ | ādāya tāni ratnāni svāṃ purīṃ punarāgatāḥ || 7.39.11 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Bharata, Lakshmana, and Shatrughna, those mighty ones, taking those jewels, came back again to their own city.

shlokas.sanskrit: आगम्य च पुरीं रम्यामयोध्यां पुरुषर्षभाः । तानि रत्नानि चित्राणि रामाय समुपाहरन् ।। 7.39.12 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: āgamya ca purīṃ ramyāmayodhyāṃ puruṣarṣabhāḥ | tāni ratnāni citrāṇi rāmāya samupāharan || 7.39.12 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: And having reached the lovely city of Ayodhya, those bulls among men presented those wondrous jewels to Rama.

shlokas.sanskrit: प्रतिगृह्य च तत्सर्वं रामः प्रीतिसमन्वितः । सुग्रीवाय ददौ राज्ञे महात्मा कृतकर्मणे ।। 7.39.13 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: pratigṛhya ca tatsarvaṃ rāmaḥ prītisamanvitaḥ | sugrīvāya dadau rājñe mahātmā kṛtakarmaṇe || 7.39.13 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Receiving all of it, Rama, the great-souled one, filled with affection, gave it to King Sugriva, who had accomplished the deed.

shlokas.sanskrit: बिभीषणाय च ददौ तथान्येभ्यो ऽपि राघवः । राक्षसेभ्यः कपिभ्यश्च यैर्वृतो जयमाप्तवान् ।। 7.39.14 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: bibhīṣaṇāya ca dadau tathānyebhyo 'pi rāghavaḥ | rākṣasebhyaḥ kapibhyaśca yairvṛto jayamāptavān || 7.39.14 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: And Raghava gave to Vibhishana as well, and to the others too, to the Rakshasas and the monkeys, surrounded by whom he had won the victory.

shlokas.sanskrit: ते सर्वे रामदत्तानि रत्नानि कपिराक्षसाः । शिरोभिर्धारयामासुर्बाहुभिश्च महाबलाः ।। 7.39.15 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: te sarve rāmadattāni ratnāni kapirākṣasāḥ | śirobhirdhārayāmāsurbāhubhiśca mahābalāḥ || 7.39.15 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: All those monkeys and Rakshasas, the mighty ones, bore upon their heads and in their arms the jewels given by Rama.

shlokas.sanskrit: हनूमन्तं च नृपतिरिक्ष्वाकूणां महारथः । अङ्गदं च महाबाहुमङ्कमारोप्य वीर्यवान् ।। 7.39.16 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: hanūmantaṃ ca nṛpatirikṣvākūṇāṃ mahārathaḥ | aṅgadaṃ ca mahābāhumaṅkamāropya vīryavān || 7.39.16 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: And the king of the Ikshvakus, the great chariot-warrior, the valiant one, having set Hanuman and the mighty-armed Angada upon his lap,

shlokas.sanskrit: रामः कमलपत्राक्षः सुग्रीवमिदमब्रवीत् । अङ्गदस्ते सुपुत्रो ऽयं मन्त्री चाप्यनिलात्मजः ।। 7.39.17 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: rāmaḥ kamalapatrākṣaḥ sugrīvamidamabravīt | aṅgadaste suputro 'yaṃ mantrī cāpyanilātmajaḥ || 7.39.17 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Rama, whose eyes were like lotus petals, spoke thus to Sugriva: "This Angada is your good son, and the son of the Wind-god is your counselor."

shlokas.sanskrit: सुग्रीवमन्त्रिते युक्तौ मम चापि हिते रतौ । अर्हतो विविधां पूजां त्वत्कृते वै हरीश्वर ।। 7.39.18 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: sugrīvamantrite yuktau mama cāpi hite ratau | arhato vividhāṃ pūjāṃ tvatkṛte vai harīśvara || 7.39.18 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: "These two, devoted to Sugriva's counsel and intent likewise upon my welfare, deserve manifold honor for your sake, O lord of the monkeys."

shlokas.sanskrit: इत्युक्त्वा व्यवमुच्याङ्गाद्भूषणानि महायशाः । स बबन्ध महार्हाणि तदाङ्गदहनूमतोः ।। 7.39.19 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: ityuktvā vyavamucyāṅgādbhūṣaṇāni mahāyaśāḥ | sa babandha mahārhāṇi tadāṅgadahanūmatoḥ || 7.39.19 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Having spoken thus, the greatly renowned one stripped the ornaments from his own body and bound those most precious jewels upon Angada and Hanuman.

shlokas.sanskrit: आभाष्य च महावीर्यान्राघवो यूथपर्षभान् । नीलं नलं केसरिणं कुमुदं गन्धमादनम् ।। 7.39.20 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: ābhāṣya ca mahāvīryānrāghavo yūthaparṣabhān | nīlaṃ nalaṃ kesariṇaṃ kumudaṃ gandhamādanam || 7.39.20 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: And Raghava addressed the mighty bulls among the troop-leaders: Nila, Nala, Kesarin, Kumuda, and Gandhamadana,

shlokas.sanskrit: सुषेणं पनसं वीरं मैन्दं द्विविदमेव च । जाम्बवन्तं गवाक्षं च विनतं धूम्रमेव च ।। 7.39.21 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: suṣeṇaṃ panasaṃ vīraṃ maindaṃ dvividameva ca | jāmbavantaṃ gavākṣaṃ ca vinataṃ dhūmrameva ca || 7.39.21 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: the valiant Sushena, Panasa, Mainda and Dvivida, Jambavan and Gavaksha, Vinata and Dhumra,

shlokas.sanskrit: वलीमुखं प्रजङ्घं च सन्नादं च महाबलम् । दरीमुखं दधिमुखमिन्द्रजानुं च यूथपम् ।। 7.39.22 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: valīmukhaṃ prajaṅghaṃ ca sannādaṃ ca mahābalam | darīmukhaṃ dadhimukhamindrajānuṃ ca yūthapam || 7.39.22 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Valimukha and Prajangha, the mighty Sannada, Darimukha, Dadhimukha, and the troop-leader Indrajanu.

shlokas.sanskrit: मधुरं श्लक्ष्णया वाचा नेत्राभ्यामापिबन्निव । सुहृदो मे भवन्तश्च शरीरं भ्रातरस्तथा ।। 7.39.23 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: madhuraṃ ślakṣṇayā vācā netrābhyāmāpibanniva | suhṛdo me bhavantaśca śarīraṃ bhrātarastathā || 7.39.23 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Sweetly, with gentle speech, as if drinking them in with his eyes, he said: "You are my dear friends, and like brothers, my very own body.

shlokas.sanskrit: युष्माभिरुद्धृतश्चाहं व्यसनात्काननौकसः । धन्यो राजा च सुग्रीवो भवद्भिः सुहृदां वरैः ।। 7.39.24 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: yuṣmābhiruddhṛtaścāhaṃ vyasanātkānanaukasaḥ | dhanyo rājā ca sugrīvo bhavadbhiḥ suhṛdāṃ varaiḥ || 7.39.24 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: By you I, a dweller in the forest, was lifted out of calamity; and King Sugriva too is blessed in having you, the best of friends."

shlokas.sanskrit: एवमुक्त्वा ददौ तेभ्यो भूषणानि यथार्हतः । वज्राणि च महार्हाणि सस्वजे च नरर्षभः ।। 7.39.25 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: evamuktvā dadau tebhyo bhūṣaṇāni yathārhataḥ | vajrāṇi ca mahārhāṇi sasvaje ca nararṣabhaḥ || 7.39.25 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Having spoken thus, the bull among men gave them ornaments according to their merit and most precious diamonds, and embraced them.

shlokas.sanskrit: ते पिबन्तः सुगन्धीनि मधूनि मधुपिङ्गलाः । मांसानि च सुमृष्टानि मूलानि च फलानि च ।। 7.39.26 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: te pibantaḥ sugandhīni madhūni madhupiṅgalāḥ | māṃsāni ca sumṛṣṭāni mūlāni ca phalāni ca || 7.39.26 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Those honey-tawny monkeys drank fragrant meads and ate well-prepared meats, roots, and fruits.

shlokas.sanskrit: एवं तेषां निवसतां मासः साग्रो ययौ तदा । मुहूर्तमिव ते सर्वे रामभक्त्या च मेनिरे ।। 7.39.27 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: evaṃ teṣāṃ nivasatāṃ māsaḥ sāgro yayau tadā | muhūrtamiva te sarve rāmabhaktyā ca menire || 7.39.27 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: While they dwelt thus, a full month and more then passed away, yet to all of them, through their devotion to Rama, it seemed but a single moment.

shlokas.sanskrit: रामो ऽपि रेमे तैः सार्धं वानरैः कामरूपिभिः । राक्षसैश्च महावीर्यैर्ऋक्षैश्चैव महाबलैः ।। 7.39.28 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: rāmo 'pi reme taiḥ sārdhaṃ vānaraiḥ kāmarūpibhiḥ | rākṣasaiśca mahāvīryairṛkṣaiścaiva mahābalaiḥ || 7.39.28 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Rama too took his delight together with those monkeys who could change their form at will, with the rakshasas of great valor, and with the mighty bears.

shlokas.sanskrit: एवं तेषां ययौ मासो द्वितीयः शिशिरः सुखम् । वानराणां प्रहृष्टानां राक्षसानां च सर्वशः ।। 7.39.29 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: evaṃ teṣāṃ yayau māso dvitīyaḥ śiśiraḥ sukham | vānarāṇāṃ prahṛṣṭānāṃ rākṣasānāṃ ca sarvaśaḥ || 7.39.29 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Thus a second month, the cool season, passed pleasantly for them, for the delighted monkeys and the rakshasas on every side.

shlokas.sanskrit: इक्ष्वाकुनगरे रम्ये परां प्रीतिमुपासताम् । रामस्य प्रीतिकरणैः कालस्तेषां सुखं ययौ ।। 7.39.30 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: ikṣvākunagare ramye parāṃ prītimupāsatām | rāmasya prītikaraṇaiḥ kālasteṣāṃ sukhaṃ yayau || 7.39.30 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Dwelling in the lovely city of the Ikshvakus, they enjoyed the highest delight; and through Rama's gracious attentions the time passed happily for them.

shlokas.sanskrit: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे एकोनचत्वारिंशः सर्गः ।। 39 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: ityārṣe śrīmadrāmāyaṇe vālmīkīye ādikāvye śrīmaduttarakāṇḍe ekonacatvāriṃśaḥ sargaḥ || 39 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Thus ends the thirty-ninth sarga in the venerable Uttara Kanda of the sacred Ramayana, the first poem, composed by the seer Valmiki.
